name: Breadboard
description: A reusable board for building circuits without solder.
purpose: Metal contacts join small groups of holes under the plastic.
useCase: Use it to prototype an LED circuit before soldering.
usage: Check connected rows with continuity mode while power is off. Rails can be split; confirm your own board.
mistake: Putting both LED legs into one connected group bypasses the LED.
activity: Trace one group of five holes with an unpowered continuity test.
referenceLabel: Breadboard contacts and rail layout

name: Resistor
description: A component that limits current and creates voltage drops.
purpose: Its resistance opposes current; it also turns electrical energy into heat.
useCase: Use a suitable resistor in series with an LED.
usage: Read the value and power rating before use. An ordinary fixed resistor works in either direction.
mistake: Choosing too little resistance can overheat the resistor or overload the LED.
activity: Decode the sample: red, red, brown, gold means 220 ohms with 5% tolerance.
referenceLabel: Resistor values and LED current limiting

name: Arduino Uno
description: A programmable board that reads inputs and controls outputs.
purpose: The Uno R3 runs your sketch and communicates through its input and output pins.
useCase: Use it for a button-controlled LED or sensor project.
usage: Check the official Uno R3 pinout. Respect voltage and current limits; use a driver for motors.
mistake: An output pin cannot supply a motor directly.
activity: Run the built-in Blink example using the onboard LED.
referenceLabel: Official Uno R3 pinout

name: 9 V battery
description: A portable DC power source with two snap terminals.
purpose: Chemical energy supplies a voltage between positive and negative terminals.
useCase: Use it for low-power projects designed for its voltage.
usage: Confirm polarity and the circuit voltage before connecting. A 9 V battery must not feed a 5 V pin directly.
mistake: Shorting the terminals can heat the battery and wires.
activity: Find the two different snap shapes and identify polarity from the actual battery.
referenceLabel: Manufacturer dimensions and terminal reference

name: LED
description: A light-emitting diode that glows when current flows in the forward direction.
purpose: It turns electrical energy into light.
useCase: Use it as a status indicator or beginner circuit output.
usage: Use a series resistor. On many new LEDs, the longer leg is the anode and the flat edge marks the cathode; confirm the datasheet.
mistake: Connecting an LED straight across a supply can destroy it.
activity: Build the separate example schematic with a suitable red LED.
referenceLabel: LED polarity and separate breadboard wiring reference

name: Pushbutton
description: A momentary switch that changes contact state while pressed.
purpose: A typical normally open tactile button joins two contact groups when pressed.
useCase: Use it to start an action or make a digital input.
usage: Four legs do not mean four independent contacts. Identify the internally joined pairs and use a pull-up or pull-down.
mistake: Wiring two already-connected legs makes the input appear permanently pressed.
activity: Test which pairs connect before and during a press, with power disconnected.
referenceLabel: Button contact groups and wiring diagram

name: Slide switch
description: A switch that stays in the position you choose.
purpose: An SPDT switch connects its common contact to either of two other contacts.
useCase: Use it to select a mode or disconnect a small load within its rating.
usage: For the referenced switch, the middle pin is common. Verify your actual part before wiring.
mistake: Treating every three-pin switch as having the same pinout can connect the wrong contacts.
activity: Use an unpowered continuity test to identify the common pin.
referenceLabel: Referenced SPDT switch contact behavior

name: Potentiometer
description: An adjustable resistor with a moving contact called a wiper.
purpose: Turning the shaft changes resistance between the wiper and each end.
useCase: Use it as an adjustable voltage divider for a control input.
usage: Identify the two ends and wiper. Keep the resulting voltage within the input rating.
mistake: Using it as a high-power motor control can damage a small potentiometer.
activity: Measure end-to-end resistance, then measure from the wiper while turning.
referenceLabel: Potentiometer construction and terminal reference

name: Piezo buzzer
description: A small sound transducer that bends a piezoelectric element.
purpose: A changing drive signal makes it vibrate and produce sound.
useCase: Use it for short tones or an alert.
usage: A passive piezo needs a changing waveform. Follow the chosen part's drive limits; active buzzers differ.
mistake: A steady DC level will not make a passive piezo play a sustained tone.
activity: Try two short tones at different frequencies.
referenceLabel: Passive piezo drive reference

name: DC motor
description: A motor that converts DC electrical energy into rotation.
purpose: Current through the motor produces torque at its shaft.
useCase: Use it to spin a fan or drive a small mechanism.
usage: Use a rated transistor or motor driver and protection for inductive switching. Keep fingers clear of the shaft.
mistake: Driving a motor from a microcontroller pin can damage the board.
activity: Study the separate transistor and flyback-diode motor circuit.
referenceLabel: Motor driver and flyback diode wiring

name: Servo motor
description: A hobby servo combines a motor, gearbox and control electronics.
purpose: A positional servo moves its output horn toward a requested position.
useCase: Use it for a small pointer or controlled mechanical movement.
usage: Its cable carries power, ground and a control signal. Verify wire colors and supply requirements for the exact model.
mistake: An undersized supply causes resets or jitter. Do not force the horn.
activity: Explore the Sweep example with the referenced wiring.
referenceLabel: Servo Sweep wiring diagram

name: Ultrasonic sensor
description: A sensor that estimates distance from an ultrasonic echo.
purpose: It sends a sound pulse and measures the time until an echo returns.
useCase: Use it for an obstacle detector or distance display.
usage: The illustrated four-pin module has supply, trigger, echo and ground. Voltage limits and pin order depend on the model.
mistake: A three-pin PING-style sensor is not wired like a four-pin HC-SR04-style module.
activity: Compare readings for a flat target at several distances.
referenceLabel: Separate module pinouts; select your exact variant

name: Temperature sensor
description: An analog sensor whose output voltage changes with temperature.
purpose: The TMP36 reports temperature as a voltage, with a built-in offset.
useCase: Use it for a room-temperature display.
usage: The TMP36 and similar-looking transistors have different functions. Use the manufacturer's package drawing to identify each lead.
mistake: Reversing supply and ground can damage the sensor.
activity: Read the output and convert it using the TMP36 datasheet equation.
referenceLabel: TMP36 package-specific manufacturer pin diagram

name: Photoresistor
description: A light-dependent resistor with two leads.
purpose: Its resistance usually falls as more light reaches its sensing surface.
useCase: Use it for a simple light-or-dark detector.
usage: Read it using a suitable voltage divider. It is not a calibrated light meter.
mistake: Connecting it alone to an analog input does not create a useful divider.
activity: Cover and uncover the sensor while observing the divider voltage.
referenceLabel: Photocell voltage-divider wiring

name: RGB LED
description: One package containing red, green and blue LED elements.
purpose: Combining their brightness levels produces different colors.
useCase: Use it for a multicolor indicator.
usage: Use a current-limiting resistor for each color channel. Confirm common-anode or common-cathode type and lead order.
mistake: One resistor on the shared lead does not control each channel independently.
activity: Compare red-only, green-only and mixed-color output.
referenceLabel: RGB LED breadboard layout; confirm your common terminal

name: Jumper wires
description: Insulated conductors that link circuit connection points.
purpose: They provide a low-resistance path between their ends.
useCase: Use male pins with breadboard sockets or female ends with header pins.
usage: Match connector type and keep exposed ends from touching unintended contacts. Color is a convention, not proof of voltage.
mistake: A loose or misplaced jumper can leave the circuit open or short two nodes.
activity: With power off, trace one connection from source to destination.
referenceLabel: Breadboard wiring and connector reference

name: Multimeter
description: An instrument for measuring electrical quantities.
purpose: Different modes measure voltage, current, resistance and often continuity.
useCase: Use it to investigate a circuit instead of guessing.
usage: Choose the correct mode and lead sockets. Measure voltage across two points; current measurement requires the appropriate series connection.
mistake: Putting a meter in current mode across a supply can create a short.
activity: Practise an unpowered continuity test first.
referenceLabel: Separate voltage, current and resistance measurement diagrams

name: Capacitor
description: A component that stores energy in an electric field.
purpose: It can smooth voltage changes and take part in timing circuits.
useCase: Use a suitable capacitor to reduce supply noise.
usage: This illustration shows a polarized electrolytic type. Check its negative stripe, voltage rating and discharge state.
mistake: Reverse polarity or excessive voltage can damage an electrolytic capacitor.
activity: Identify its marked negative lead on an unpowered, discharged part.
referenceLabel: Capacitor types, polarity and schematic reference

name: Diode
description: A component that conducts much more readily in one direction.
purpose: A rectifier diode passes forward current and blocks reverse current within its ratings.
useCase: Use an appropriate diode for rectification or inductive-load protection.
usage: The band marks the cathode on the illustrated axial rectifier. Confirm the exact part's ratings.
mistake: A flyback diode installed the wrong way can short the supply when the driver turns on.
activity: Locate the band and compare it with the schematic cathode bar.
referenceLabel: Manufacturer polarity and separate motor flyback circuit

name: NPN transistor
description: A three-terminal semiconductor used for switching or amplification.
purpose: A small base current controls a larger collector current within its operating limits.
useCase: Use a suitable NPN transistor to switch a small load.
usage: Identify base, collector and emitter from the exact datasheet. Use a base resistor and stay within device ratings.
mistake: TO-92 package shape does not guarantee the same pin order. A TMP36 sensor can look very similar.
activity: Compare the package drawing with a verified transistor driver circuit.
referenceLabel: Transistor driver diagram; match the specified transistor
